Exercise: Arm Circles

Category:
stretching

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- circular

Primary Muscles:

- shoulders

Secondary Muscles:

- traps

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
3

Energy Requirement:
low

Recovery Time:
0.5 hours

Goals:

- improve_shoulder_flexibility
- warm_up_shoulders_and_traps

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder injury, description: Avoid this exercise if you have a shoulder injury.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Larger Circles, description: Increase the diameter of the circles to 2 feet.
- name: Smaller Circles, description: Decrease the diameter of the circles to 6 inches.

Substitution Options:

- name: Arm Swings, force: push, level: beginner

Instructions:

- Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position.
- Slowly start to make circles of about 1 foot in diameter with each outstretched arm. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
- Continue the circular motion of the outstretched arms for about ten seconds. Then reverse the movement, going the opposite direction.
